metadata.title: Bias and Explainability

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for assessing and mitigating bias in AI systems, and for providing explainability and transparency of AI behavior to human stakeholders.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: AI fairness assessment, bias testing, interpretability techniques, and transparency mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern defining how AI model bias is detected and mitigated, and how AI behavior is made understandable to humans.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Provides AI-specific threat context for bias exploitation, unfair treatment, and opaque decision-making leading to harm.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats where AI models exhibit unfair outcomes due to biased training data, proxies, or structural inequities.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats where AI decisions cannot be meaningfully explained, undermining trust, accountability, and appropriate use.

metadata.remarks: Bias and Explainability defines how AI systems are assessed for fairness and how their behavior is made interpretable to human stakeholders. This pattern exists to mitigate harm from biased outcomes, support accountability, and ensure that AI-driven decisions can be understood, challenged, and responsibly relied upon.

components.title: Bias Evaluation and Monitoring
components.description: Systematic evaluation and ongoing monitoring of AI models to identify and track bias across relevant populations or contexts.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI models are evaluated for bias using appropriate metrics and monitored over time to detect regression or drift.

components.title: Explainability Mechanisms
components.description: Mechanisms that enable humans to understand, interpret, or approximate the reasoning behind AI outputs.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI systems employ explainability techniques appropriate to their context, risk, and audience to support understanding and review.

components.title: Model Cards and Documentation
components.description: Documentation describing model purpose, training context, limitations, bias considerations, and appropriate use.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI models are accompanied by documentation outlining intended use, known limitations, bias considerations, and risks.
